instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Apologize Properly
cards.instruction: Get someone to deliver the apology in the form, order, and setting you consider valid.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please apologise for eating my cake at the table where it happened. I'll come with you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry. There, I've said it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At the table, please. Walk over before you start; I don't want half an apology in each room.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your dad's sitting there. Can't we do this privately?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He heard me blame the dog. Tell him you ate it first. Then turn to me and say you're sorry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Read me the subject line of your apology email. It needs to name the vase you broke.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've put 'sorry'.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Add the incident, please. The recipient shouldn't have to open an apology to discover what it's for.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send 'Sorry about the vase' to Mum. She still thinks you broke it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the first sentence is 'I broke the vase'. Please don't make her infer who did it again.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Get It on the Record
cards.instruction: Get formal approval, endorsement, or acknowledgment before anyone can quietly revise their position.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Initial the festival budget total before lunch, please. I'll file the approved copy.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said yes. Just write my name on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can enter your name, but you supply the approval. Put your initials beside the total yourself.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I may change my mind. I'd want that copy removed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then date any replacement. We keep the first copy too; please don't confuse revising a decision with erasing it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I pay the builder, sign that my fence can stay on our boundary. I'll show you the line.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I suppose it can.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Write 'can stay', please. I can record permission; I can't record a shrug.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not promising forever.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then put today's date beside it. A later change gets another date, not an empty space where your name used to be.

cards.title: Assigned by Procedure
cards.instruction: Get someone to accept an unwanted responsibility by proving that the rules, rotation, or tradition make it theirs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's your Tuesday bin duty again. Check the rota before you leave.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I covered your Thursday last week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I covered your Tuesday. Read the swap box: one week only. We're back on our usual days.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You added that box.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because you didn't want my Thursday permanently. Please read the limit as well as the names. Your Tuesday is back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As the new club president, take the toilet keys with the office keys. I'll show you the closing checklist.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought the caretaker cleaned them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Read the minutes under 'cost savings'. Cleaning and closing went to the president when we cancelled that contract.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I proposed that when you were president.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I followed it all year. It names the office, not me. Start with the washbasins; I'll show you where the supplies go back.

cards.title: Complete the Record
cards.instruction: Get someone to fill the missing gaps in an account without revealing which answer matters most to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For the party log, fill in arrival, kitchen visit and departure. I'll check the times with you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You only care who took the cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There are three empty boxes. Begin at the top, please; I'll read them back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. Put eight for arrival, and put me down for the cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Eight goes in the first box. 'Me' isn't a time. Let's complete the kitchen box before we add comments.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The car's back. Its return log needs mileage, fuel and driver. Give me the entries in order, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You mean who dented it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I mean the whole row. Start with mileage; don't substitute a damage report for the log.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Driver I remember. The rest means six flights down to check the dashboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll go and read it. Keep the row open; we aren't skipping an entry because the stairs are inconvenient.

cards.title: Make It Official
cards.instruction: Recruit someone by giving them a title, role, or ceremonial duty that makes participation feel binding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've appointed you Keeper of the Festival Lantern. Hold it upright, please; you're representing us now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only held it while you tied your shoe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A useful trial. Keep your hand below the glass while I pin on your badge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I leave it at the ticket desk when I go?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hand it to a person, not a desk. Introduce them as the next Keeper and show them the grip before you release it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you be patron of our roof appeal? I'll guide you through thanking the donors.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll come, but I won't make a speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not wearing that ribbon. Every donor gets the same applause. Keep your place beside me; I'll give you each cue.
